resulting_evidence:
The existing `export.py` already quotes commas correctly, so no code change is needed. I did not run the test. This evaluation is read-only, so the result below comes from reading the code against the test.

`csv.writer` defaults to `QUOTE_MINIMAL` and `lineterminator='\r\n'`. For `[["a,b", "c"]]` it writes `"a,b",c\r\n`, which is exactly what `test_commas` asserts. A new helper, a dependency or a rewrite would add complexity without changing behavior, so the stdlib `csv` module is the simplest suitable implementation for this project. `project.md` also says no new dependency is required.

Routing: this is not a new library or integration choice, and the existing stdlib module settles the question locally. I did not activate `search-first` or do web research.

One caveat for callers: `csv` writes `\r\n` itself, so when a caller passes a file, open it with `newline=''`. Otherwise, on Windows, text mode can produce `\r\r\n`. The test uses `StringIO`, so it does not catch this.

Next action: run `python -m pytest test_export.py` from the project folder to confirm the test passes.
